_comment: Golden table for composite-secret rendering (Phase 24.1), which exists
twice: src/ts/composite.ts (the form's live preview, which has to render
on every keystroke) and vault-core/src/composite.rs (the CLI and the app,
over IPC — see CLAUDE.md's twin-pair table for why the app asks Rust
tests/composite.test.ts pins the TypeScript side; vault-core's
tests/composite_parity.rs pins the Rust side against the identical cases.
Reviewing two renderers for agreement does not work — same arrangement,
same reason, as totp-seeds.json and env-names.json.
Each case renders `template` with `kind` against `parts` (an object,
key -> raw value). A successful case has `out: {text, used, unused}`; a
refused one has `error: {kind, name?, at?}` and no `out`.

render._why: The motivating case: a calendar URL with a userinfo-zone part and a path-zone part.
A Discord webhook: two path-segment parts, nothing else in the URL to confuse the classifier.
Userinfo encoding is mandatory: a raw '@' or ':' in the password would otherwise move the host boundary (postgres://app:p@ss@db/prod parses with host ss@db).
A query value containing a space and a query name that is itself a part, both percent-encoded — this is the '${scope}=bot applications.commands' shape from the design.
A fragment-zone part, encoded like every other zone.
'{{' and '}}' are literal braces, not an empty placeholder.
One placeholder used twice is one part filled in both places (C3), not two parts.
A part no placeholder uses is reported, never an error — the caller (health scan, form) decides what to do with it.
custom never encodes — what is copied is exactly what was typed, slashes and spaces included.
An unrecognised kind string behaves like custom — assuming URL structure over an unknown shape corrupts a value as easily as it protects one.
An unfilled placeholder refuses to render rather than producing a URL with a hole in it.
An unbalanced '{' is a form error, not a literal brace.
A stray '}' with no opening '{' is refused the same way.
A newline in a part is refused for a URL-shaped kind (C6) — a link with an embedded newline is not a link.
The same control character is allowed for custom — not every composite is a URL.
